AGENDA

Meetings are broadcast live on Glendale TV, viewable on Spectrum Cable, channel 6, and AT&T U-
verse, channel 99. Meetings are also streamed live in high definition (HD) on the city's webpage,
glendaleca.gov/live, on YouTube.com/myglendale, and on Apple TV, Roku, and Amazon Fire
devices using a free app called Screenweave and choosing “Glendale TV” from the menu. Meetings
are also archived on the City Website for viewing anytime at glendaleca.gov/agendas. Call (818)
548-4013 for program schedules. DVDs of the proceedings are available for purchase in the City
Clerk's Office. For public comments and questions during the meeting, call (818) 937-8100. Public
comments on a specific agenda item will be taken when that agenda item is discussed. If you have
any question about matters on the agenda, or requests for assistance, please contact the City Clerk
at (818) 548-2090 during regular business hours.
  PLEASE TURN OFF CELLULAR PHONES WHILE INSIDE THE MEETING LOCATION
In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) of 1990, auxiliary hearing aids, sign
language translation, and Braille transcripts are available upon request. Assisted listening devices
are available same-day upon request. At least 48 hours (or two business days) notice is required for
requests regarding sign language translation and Braille transcription services. All documents
related to open session items on this agenda that are received less than 72 hours prior to this
meeting, and are public records, will be available for review in the Office of the City Clerk, 613 E.
Broadway, RM 110, Glendale, CA 91206.
Translation services are provided for meetings through the use of bilingual staff for speakers who
wish to utilize the service as available. Speakers should state their request by contacting the City
Clerk’s office at (818) 548-2090, at least 24 hours prior to the scheduled meeting. Please specify
the language for which you require translation. The exclusive use of City provided interpreters is not
required and persons are welcome to use their own interpreter or speak in their native language.

5. CITY COUNCIL/STAFF COMMENTS
  City Manager Roubik Golanian pulled item 7b off the agenda.

  Public Works Director Yazdan Emrani announced a second compost giveaway on November
  5th at Parking Lot 30 on North Verdugo Road, following a successful compost giveaway on
  October 1st.

  Police Lt. Alex Krikorian announced that the Glendale Health Fair will offer free Heart Health
  Education Classes and the 11th Annual Glendale Health Festival will provide free dental,
  vision, and medical care for children and adults on November 5-6 at Pacific Community
  Center.

  City Clerk Suzie Abajian stated the Glendale City Clerk’s office, in collaboration with the Los
  Angeles County Registrar Recorder’s Office, hosted a mobile vote center at City Hall Plaza.
  She thanked the City of Glendale employees and the public who came out to vote. Abajian
  provided a brief report on vote-by-mail drop-off locations and voting centers leading up to the
  November 8th elections.

  Councilmember Devine announced there will be an opening for the GWP Commission and
  asked members of the public who are interested to send their application to the City Clerk’s
  office. She thanked and congratulated Diane Evers and company who organized the Virginia
  11 01 22
  CC

  3
   Avenue Fall Festival for their neighborhood. Devine asked staff to send a condolence letter to
  the Consul General of the Republic of Korea of Los Angeles, Kim Youngwan, regarding the
  horrific loss of life over the Halloween tragedy in South Korea. Kassakhian seconded. She
  announced it is Native American Heritage Month and asked to celebrate our indigenous
  community by thanking and acknowledging their accomplishments and contributions to our
  city, state, and country.

  Councilmember Asatryan announced on Thursday the Commission on the Status of Women
  and the YWCA of Glendale and Pasadena held a beautiful candlelight vigil and purple tie
  event honoring men in our community who take action and go above and beyond, spreading
  awareness and helping with domestic violence issues. She stated that she would like to use
  this opportunity to also provide information to anybody that needs help. Asatryan stated they
  are not alone and there are a lot of resources available from legal assistance, shelter,
  housing, food pantry, etc. She mentioned that YWCA Glendale can be reached at
  818.242.4155, crisis hotline at 888.999.7511, and the LA County 24/7 hotline at 800.978.3600.
  She asked the public to reach out if they need assistance.

  Councilmember Najarian indicated there used to be another public swimming pool in
  Glendale, besides the Pacific Community Pool, by the Glendale Community College called
  “keyhole,” which was paved and converted into a parking lot. He asked staff to provide a
  report and see if there are any locations which would be suitable for another public swimming
  pool. Asatryan seconded.

  Councilmember Brotman followed-up on the re-appointment of Sevana Zadorian for the Arts
  and Culture Commission. City Manager Roubik Golanian indicated that it will be agendized for
  the November 15, 2022 Council Meeting.

  Mayor Kassakhian invited the public to attend the Veterans Day Memorial Event on November
  11 at Forest Lawn Hollywood Hills. He asked to revive the Veterans Committee that used to
  organize the memorial and veteran’s day events and asked the veterans out there to reach
  out to the City Manager’s office if they wish to volunteer. Kassakhian stated that the City of
  Glendale was voted before as one of the best communities to go trick or treating in for
  Halloween and mentioned few of the neighborhoods in the city that had Halloween events for
  children. Mayor Kassakhian reminded the public to turn in their vote-by-mail ballots. He also
  announced that for those who want to learn more about the Native American heritage, there
  are a number of great programs that are happening through Glendale Library, Arts, and
  Culture.
